Relays are dual-connected where they have two ports; otherwise to core A only. AH8 (NECR) has no relay communication; it is hardwired to row 1.
I/O rows (SICAM I/O link, not through the switches)
Rows 1 and 2: CI-8532 on copper inside the SCADA cabinet
Rows 3 to 6: CI-8533 on dedicated fibre pairs in the same trench cables as the ring
Both controllers connect to every row (Siemens to confirm)
No routing between VLANs: the CP-8050 is the only device with ports in more than one zone. FW-01 is the only route to the outside.
Core A → SW-MV → SW-BESS → SW-GEN → SW-PRS → SW-PMS → core B · one break isolates nothing
Each field switch: 2 SFP single-mode ring ports and at least 6 copper ports. Patch panels at both ends of every fibre route.
Fibre routes: switchroom – President, switchroom – PM, President – PM (closes the ring); yard and generator area on spare cores. Lengths from the cable route drawings.
Rows 5 and 6 use spare fibre cores in the cables to SW-BESS and SW-GEN; rows 3 and 4 in the cables to the office stations.
TABLE A – VLAN AND IP PLAN (PROPOSED)
SCADA: SRV-A/B, OWS-01, ENG-01, FW-01 inside, CP-8050 X1
Substation: relays AH1–AH7, PM5560 ×3, MGate ×2, DG controllers, CP-8050 X3
Monitoring: PLC box, blue'Log XM, UPS, GPS-01, CP-8050 X4
Switch management: core and field switches

Device; stripe = link type to the SCADA
Read with sheet 001. Addresses and port numbers are proposals for approval; final
values are fixed in the IP plan at the factory test.
All switches managed: unused ports disabled, port security, SNMP v3 and syslog to
SRV-A/B, HTTPS and SSH management on VLAN 99.
No routing between VLANs. The CP-8050 is the only device with ports in more than one
zone (CI-8520), and FW-01 is the only route to the outside.
Ring protocol and recovery time are set at configuration (Moxa Turbo Ring or RSTP).
I/O rows 3 to 6 run on dedicated fibre pairs (CI-8533), separate from the ring.
Siemens to confirm whether they can be laid as a ring.
